Use OpenBLAS 0.3.30 with the specified configuration, install SciPy from the buggy commit cbef678e05c5, run the specific linregress test that asserts NaN inference for the two-point case; it fails on buggy and passes on the fixed revision where the PR changes expected results.

strategy.reproducing_test: test_linregress_two_points_nan_inference (adds gh-24684 coverage): constructs x=[0.,1.], y=[0.,1.], calls stats.linregress(x,y), then asserts res.pvalue, res.stderr, res.intercept_stderr are NaN (while slope/intercept remain correct).
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision cbef678e05c5, `xp_assert_equal(res.pvalue, NaN)`, `xp_assert_equal(res.stderr, NaN)`, or `xp_assert_equal(res.intercept_stderr, NaN)` fails because the results are `0.0` (i.e., zero is returned instead of NaN for the two-point degenerate degrees-of-freedom case). On the fixed revision (the PR that implements the NaN inference behavior from gh-24684), the same assertions pass because `pvalue`, `stderr`, and `intercept_stderr` are `NaN`.
strategy.numerical_probe: None required beyond the test above; the transition is decided entirely by whether those three fields are NaN vs 0.0 for x=[0.,1.], y=[0.,1.].

This test likely should be backend-independent (pure Python/NumPy computations), but SciPy may use different code paths depending on array API backend (`xp` fixture). Ensure you run under the same `xp` setting used by SciPy’s test suite (typically NumPy; the test uses the `xp` fixture).

Platform/toolchain: requires building SciPy; differences in compilers/optimization flags could theoretically affect floating-point handling. Use the same compiler family/flags as your CI baseline if possible.

oracle.reference_source: SciPy PR/test update described in the provided diff and issue evidence (gh-24684): asserts exact NaN equality for res.pvalue, res.stderr, res.intercept_stderr when n==2 degenerate case.
oracle.why: The test uses `xp_assert_equal` to compare to `xp.asarray(xp.nan)`, so the oracle is exact (NaN vs not-NaN), not tolerance-based.
